entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antoine Bohier Du Prat was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal, born in France around 1485 and died on December 7, 1519.

As a prominent figure in the Catholic Church during the Renaissance, Du Prat played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation, working to restore Catholic orthodoxy in France.

Du Prat's influence extended beyond his theological pursuits, as he was also a patron of the arts and architecture, commissioning numerous projects in France and Italy.

Despite his significant contributions to the Catholic Church, Du Prat's legacy is often overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and he remains a relatively lesser-known figure in historical accounts.

Du Prat's life and work continue to be studied by historians and scholars seeking to understand the complexities of the Catholic Church during this pivotal period in European history.

The exact dates of Du Prat's birth and early life are unknown, adding to the enigmatic nature of his historical figure.
